title: Violin lessons and what he played on violin
summary: He studied violin with Professor William Nickerson at Southern, still plays, and recalls playing classics, jazz and rags like Maple Leaf Rag.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: I'd sing it just one at a time. And Professor William Nickerson, he taught me violin. I take violin lessons from Professor William Nickerson.
Was that at Southern or at Fifth?
Yeah. That's Southern. That's on that magazine.
Mm-hmm. You still play violin? Yeah, I still play violin. You ought to go down to Bill Russell's shop and play a little for him.
Well, I used to be master once. It's been so long. Violin is an instrument that if you stay away from it longer, I'd stay away from it. But I used to be one of the greatest of it.
What tunes did you play on the violin?

Oh, classics, semi-classics, popular jazz, swing. People used to stop dancing on the floor. People would stop dancing, come walking by the music stand. Stop. Turn the gun or lose. Stop. Come stand up out of the stand, look at me playing.
You don't remember any tunes that particularly were featured on the violin in those days? Oh, I used to be black and white.

I used to be rubber plant. It was tough in that day. Rubber plant, you just heard talking that day, yeah? Rubber plant, that was tough in that day. That's a rag. Oh, yeah. Yes. Maple Leaf Rag. They're talking that day.
